sentences.text: Alanqa possessed straight, pointed jaws that resembled those of the pterosaurs Quetzalcoatlus and Zhejiangopterus.
Bony bumps on the jaw hint at unique functions, perhaps for display, muscle attachment, or crushing hard food.
The name Alanqa derives from the Arabic term al-'anqā', a mythical bird comparable to the Persian Simurgh.
Comparisons with related species suggest that individuals known from jaw specimens likely possessed wingspans of about 4 meters.
The type locality of Alanqa is Aferdou N'Chaft, located about 10 km northeast of Taouz near the village of Begaa.
Paleontologists excavated sites in the Kem Kem Beds with local villagers' assistance in April and November to December 2008.
A rostrum fragment described in 2015 was referred to Alanqa based on its origin.
Alanqa was likely prey for large predators including Spinosaurus, Carcharodontosaurus, Sauroniops, Aegisuchus, and possibly an unidentified madtsoiid snake.
According to Ibrahim and colleagues, a vertebra likely from the same species suggests an individual with a wingspan of about 6 meters.
Alanqa was initially classified in the Azhdarchidae based on jaw similarities to Quetzalcoatlus and Zhejiangopterus.
A 2022 study recovered Alanqa as a basal azhdarchoid related to Keresdrakon, forming the new clade Alanqidae.
Alanqa lived about 95 million years ago during the Cenomanian in what is now southeastern Morocco.
The animal inhabited a freshwater delta system during the late Cenomanian.
A 2018 analysis suggested Alanqa was a thalassodromid, but this classification is not well-supported.
